newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore government bonds close higher.
newsitem.headline: Singapore government bonds close higher.

text.p: Singapore government bonds closed higher on Monday in moderate trade on interbank and retail interest, dealers said.
"Bond prices were marked down slightly today following a small hike in the interbank rate. Treasury bill yields were slightly higher. Volume was moderate," a local dealer said.
Among bonds, April 1999 ended at S$98.53/98.63 compared with last Friday's close of S$98.60/98.65, May 2002 at S$99.42/99.52 against S$99.55/99.60 and June 2003 at S$94.43/94.53 from S$94.58/94.63.
The overnight interbank offered rate rose to 2-1/2 2-3/8 percent versus last Friday's 2 1-7/8 percent.
In treasury bills, three-months closed at a yield of 2.83/2.78 percent against last Friday's yield of 2.65/2.60 percent and one-year at a yield of 2.68/2.63 percent from 2.63/2.58 percent.
